# Modular Outerwear Devices
MODsuits are back-mounted sealed suits that deploy a helmet, chestplate, gauntlets and boots from a control unit. Parts, plating, cores and modules are printed at the [bold]Exosuit Fabricator[/bold] after researching [bold]Modular Technologies[/bold]; department-specific modules and plating are printed at the department techfabs.
## Assembling a MODsuit
1. Print a [bold]MOD shell[/bold], [bold]MOD core[/bold], [bold]MOD helmet[/bold], [bold]MOD chestplate[/bold], [bold]MOD gauntlets[/bold], [bold]MOD boots[/bold] and a [bold]plating[/bold]. 2. Click the shell with the core to insert it, then [bold]screwdriver[/bold] the core in place. 3. Click the shell with the helmet, then the chestplate, the gauntlets and the boots. 4. [bold]Wrench[/bold] the assembly, then [bold]screwdriver[/bold] it. 5. Add the plating, then wrench the finished unit. The plating decides the suit's appearance, armour and complexity cap. 6. Wear the control unit on your back.
## Using the suit
- Right-click the control unit and pick [bold]MOD interface[/bold] to see its parts, modules, complexity and charge. The interface works while worn or on the ground. - Use the [bold]Deploy MOD parts[/bold] action to deploy or retract the four parts, then [bold]Toggle MOD activation[/bold] to seal the suit. - All parts must be deployed before sealing, and modules cannot be installed or removed while the suit is active. The maintenance panel also has to be open. - Modules require the parts they list and count against the suit's complexity. A module cannot be installed if it duplicates an existing one or would exceed the cap. - The suit's drain plus every module's idle and active draw comes out of the battery in the core. When the battery empties the suit cuts power and slows the wearer until it is charged or replaced. - To swap the cell, open the panel with a [bold]screwdriver[/bold] and use the [bold]Remove power cell[/bold] verb. To take the core out, open the panel and hit the unit with a [bold]wrench[/bold].
## Cores
- [bold]Standard core[/bold]: takes a power cell and holds 1 MJ at full charge. - [bold]Microreactor core[/bold]: sealed, holds 1.08 MJ and slowly recharges itself. - [bold]Plasma core[/bold]: holds 720 kJ and is refuelled by feeding it plasma sheets.
## Modules
Modules are printed at the Exosuit Fabricator and unlocked by research. They include storage, flashlights, welding and medical visors, health analysers, GPS, injectors, defibrillators, patient transport, jetpacks, magboots, clamps, drills, holsters, cloaks, energy shields, EMP shielding, radiation protection, t-ray scanners, a chameleon projector and many more. Department techfabs sell their own themed modules and plating, and some themes come with built-in modules that cannot be removed.
## Built-in themes
- [bold]Loader[/bold]: hydraulic arms, a loader clamp and a hydraulic magnet, worn by the Quartermaster. - [bold]Mining[/bold]: sphere transform and ash accretion, for asteroid work. - [bold]Syndicate[/bold] and [bold]Elite[/bold]: flash protection, night vision and insulation built in.
The [bold]MOD interface[/bold] lists every installed module, its complexity and draw, and lets you use, toggle, pin or eject it.
